newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES FIRMER DESPITE LIQUIDITY.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES FIRMER DESPITE LIQUIDITY.

text.p: Short-term trading rates on Zimbabwe's money market were quoted firmer on Monday despite a surplus of cash in the system, dealers said.
"The market is expected to be liquid today and tomorrow but rates are still going up," one dealer said.
Market analysts say most players are keen to see firmer rates, in line with inflationary levels currently around 19.9 percent.
On Monday, the central Reserve Bank auctioned liquidity control treasury bills worth Z$100 million at a yield of 19.43 percent, up from 19 percent at a similar sale on Friday.

Negotiable certificates of deposit maturing after 30, 60 and 90 days were being bought at 20.5 percent from 20 and bankers acceptance bills added a percentage point to 20 percent. Call money was at 18 percent, up from 17 percent.
Reserve Bank figures indicated an unsettled market surplus of Z$43 million for Saturday.
